g.text: Figure 3a · A useful action graph with a role error
Published narrative · Lewis Carroll, Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, Chapter I · B output

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_3a_alice_actions'; text-anchor: start; fill: #142d40
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_3a_alice_actions'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having
nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it
had no pictures or conversations in it, “and what is the use of a book,” thought Alice

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_3a_alice_actions'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: So she was considering in her own mind (as well as she could, for the hot day made her
feel very sleepy and stupid), whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be
worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a White Rabbit
with pink eyes ran close by her.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Paper-figure_3a_alice_actions'; text-anchor: start; fill: #315d82

g.text: Which sitting/location, reading/inspection and running relationships involve Alice, her sister,
the book, bank and Rabbit? Exclude thoughts, feelings, appearance and book-content
